findings.title: Null deref when destinationCalendar is empty and location is Google Meet
findings.body: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` yields `undefined` when the array is empty or null, but the next line reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining. Bookings with a Meet location and no destination calendar will throw a TypeError instead of falling back to Cal Video. Use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

findings.title: Team destination calendars lost when the organizer has none
findings.body: `evt.destinationCalendar` is set to null when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar. `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is then a no-op, so collective team members' calendars are silently dropped. It also mutates the array that was just built. Initialise to `[]` and push into it.

findings.title: Event type destination calendar overrides the organizer's, and the first item is persisted as the booking's
findings.body: When the event type has a destination calendar, the organizer's own calendar is not added. For a collective event whose first calendar is a team member's or the event type's, the booking record connects only `destinationCalendar[0]`, which may not be the organizer's. Reschedule and cancel flows that fall back to booking.destinationCalendar then point at the wrong calendar.

findings.title: loadUsers rewrite drops organization select and throws for dynamic groups
findings.body: The `organization: { select: { slug } }` selection was removed from the dynamic-user query, which may break code that reads `user.organization`. A new throw was added when `dynamicUserList` is empty, and errors are mapped to a generic 500 "Unable to load users". This is an unrelated behavioural change to user loading that is not described in the PR.

findings.title: Fallback lookup is a no-op
findings.body: In updateEvent and deleteEvent the fallback is `destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. It runs only when externalCalendarId is falsy and compares against that same falsy value, so it can never find anything meaningful. The fallback to a destination calendar is effectively removed. In updateEvent this leaves calendarId undefined.

findings.title: Unrelated inversion of slug logic
findings.body: The change flips `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug }` to `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}`. The slug is now set on the org only when team billing is enabled, where before it was set only when billing was disabled. This reverses behaviour and is unrelated to destination calendars.

findings.title: Inconsistent e2e expectations for destinationCalendar
findings.body: Only the BOOKING_REJECTED expectation was changed to `[]`. The BOOKING_CREATED and BOOKING_REQUESTED tests still expect `destinationCalendar: null`. No tests cover the new multi-host behaviour.
